description:
Change an animation's code: ONE revision, checked and probed in a sandbox. Each direct save returns a contact sheet (preview: false skips; preview: true or {entry, timestamps, filmstrip, ...} looks closer; preview_warnings).

The server holds the files; keep no local copy. Create with each file's full text once, then edit the saved revision:
  files: [{path, content}]  new file or rewrite
  files: [{path, edits: [{old, new, replace_all?}]}]  a change
  edits: [{op: delete|move, path, to?}]
On disk: patch (git diff) · {path, patch} · {path, upload_id} · upload_ids from upload_file.
A non-matching edit, or code that fails to parse or build, saves nothing (saved: false; retry from the same base_rev). files_changed has sha256s.

Before writing animation code, read get_design_guide({topic: "animation"}); before writing any helper, search the stdlib with get_design_guide({topic: "stdlib", query}).
Hard rules: code never reads voiceover words; one cue per story moment, set from word timings, small things timed from it; render is deterministic (no state between frames, randomness only from the seed).

CREATE IN PLACE: animation:'new' (scope, name, slug) + project_id + place: {clip_index} places it on the first passing save and returns element_id; then edit by element_id + project_id (saves update the editor live). More entries: place: {clip_index, entry}, no changes needed.
WHILE DRAFTING, PASS project_id: passing saves move its uses; without it uses_behind names projects that "will see an update available" and the animation.update_uses call. checkpoint: '<note>' keeps a version.

Reply: rev, saved, probe, checks, errors, files_changed, element_id, uses_moved, uses_behind, note; detail: 'full' adds hunks and thumbnails. Imports stay pinned (dependency_updates: animation.bump('<animation>', '<alias>')); project-scope importers re-pin (dependents_updated).

Refusals: stale_base, target_required ('shared'|'fork'), check_failed. Settings, actions, cues: update_elements({updates:[{element_id, cues:[{op:'set', key, t}]}]}).

animation.description: The animation to edit when there is no element: @org/<slug> or an id. 'new' creates one (then pass scope, name and slug).

base_rev.description: The revision you read and expect to edit from. If it has moved, the save is refused with stale_base, the current revision and the files changed since.

checkpoint.description: A one-line note that saves this revision, when it passes, as a version in the element's history in the editor (the user can preview and restore it there). Set it when you reach a state worth returning to, not on every draft.

detail.description: summary (default) returns the outcome and what changed; full adds the diff hunks and every probe thumbnail.

dry_run.description: Build and check the edits without saving. Returns a `preview` token; render it with get_clip(render: {preview}).

edits.description: Operations, applied in order before `files`: delete and move (replace and write also work; files is the shorter way).

all.description: replace: replace every occurrence instead of requiring one.

new.description: replace: the text to put in its place.

old.description: replace: the exact text to find, copied from read_animation.

op.description: replace: exact-match `old` → `new` in `path` (fails unless `old` occurs exactly once, or pass all: true). write: create or overwrite `path` with `content`. delete: remove `path`. move: rename `path` to `to`.

path.description: File path inside the animation, e.g. 'entries/maya.js'.

element_id.description: The animation element this edit is about. The edit starts from the revision that element shows, and every use in this project moves to the new revision when it passes.

files.description: Per-file changes, each with exactly one of edits, content, patch or upload_id. Applied in order after `edits` and `patch`, all saved as ONE revision.

content.description: The whole file: a new file, or a full rewrite.

edits.description: Search-and-replace edits for an existing file, applied in order (each sees the text the one before left). Prefer these over content for changes to existing files.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

old.description: The exact text to find, copied from read_animation without the 'N| ' line numbers. Must occur exactly once unless replace_all.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one.

patch.description: A unified diff of this one file ('@@ -a,b +c,d @@' hunks). Context and removed lines must match exactly; a hunk may sit at other line numbers.

path.description: File path inside the animation, e.g. 'entries/maya.js'.

upload_id.description: The mcp_upload_id (mup_…) of a text file sent with upload_file (file_name + its curl), used as the whole content, so a big file never goes inline. UTF-8 text, at most 256 KB.

folder.description: Only with animation 'new' and scope 'library' (a save the user asked to keep for the workspace): the library folder, by path, e.g. 'Characters' or 'Characters/Presenters'. Missing folders are created (at most three levels).

name.description: Only with animation 'new': the display name.

patch.description: For a client working from files on disk: a unified diff of any number of files against the saved revision (`git diff`, `diff -u` or `diff -ruN`), run from the folder holding manifest.json. The server holds the base. New files (--- /dev/null), deletes and renames apply too. A hunk whose context no longer matches is refused with the saved lines around it; nothing is saved.

place.description: Put the animation on the canvas on the first passing save, as an animation element on this clip (the add_elements placement), and return its element_id: pass that on every later edit so each passing save updates the editor live. Needs project_id. Placing is per entry and clip: an entry already on that clip is not placed again (its element_id comes back); any other entry, or the same entry on another clip, is, and existing elements keep their own entries. Works for an existing animation too (animation: '@org/<slug>', or element_id + place.entry for another entry of the element's animation), and with no file changes at all it only places the latest revision. A failing save places nothing.

clip_index.description: Zero-based clip the animation belongs to. With continue_from: the clip it continues into (default the next).

continue_from.description: An animation element on an earlier clip that this one carries on from across the cut: placed in its box. The same animation, or a fork of it, picks up at the second it reached (timing 'trim'); any other starts at its own 0 with its own settings.

end_time.description: Seconds from the clip's start (default: the clip's end).

entry.description: Which entry to place (default: the only one, else 'main', else the first). Any entry not yet on that clip is placed, also of an animation already on the canvas.

height.description: Box height, canvas pixels (default: the full canvas).

width.description: Box width, canvas pixels (default: the full canvas).

actions.description: Action clips to try, [{name, start, duration?, args?}], element-local seconds; duration defaults to the action's default_duration. Replaces the element's clips for this render.

cues.description: Cue times to try, key: seconds (element-local).

duration.description: How long the entry plays in the preview, in seconds.

entry.description: Which entry to show (default: the element's, or the animation's first).

around.description: Center the window on a cue ('cue:land') or an action clip ('action:hop', by name or id) instead of from/to. On a whole clip, a cue several animations share is 'cue:land@<element name>'.

fps.description: Frames per second instead of a count, e.g. 8 over 2 s is 17, capped at 16.

frames.description: How many frames across the window, first and last included (default 12, max 16).

from.description: Window start, element-local seconds, or clip seconds for a whole clip (default 0).

seam.description: get_clip of a whole clip only: the cut from this clip into the next, as the player shows it: this clip's last second, its transition, and the next clip's first second, in this clip's seconds; takes frames, no window. Every cut of the film at once: get_project({render: {seams: true}}).

span.description: With around: the window's length in seconds (default 2 around a cue; the clip plus 0.5 around an action).

to.description: Window end, element-local seconds, or clip seconds for a whole clip (default the end).

filmstrip.description: See motion in ONE image instead of four moments: frames spaced evenly across a window (default 12 over the whole animation), in reading order, each labelled with its element-local time, with a thin timeline under each row marking the frames, cues (lines) and action clips (bars). Read pacing, easing and whether a beat lands on its cue from it. true for the defaults, or {from, to} / {around: 'cue:<key>' | 'action:<name>', span}, with frames or fps. Replaces timestamps. On get_clip without element_id, animation or preview it shows the whole clip, every element drawn, in clip seconds, and the timeline also ticks each element's start and end.

param_tracks.description: Keyframed settings to try, key: [{t, value, interpolation?}], t in element-local seconds. Replaces that key's track for this render.

parameter_values.description: Settings to render with, merged over the element's own (key: value).

timestamps.description: Moments to show, element-local seconds (default four across its length).

video.description: For people: also a short low-resolution MP4 of the same window (the filmstrip's, or the animation's first 10 s), returned as video_url, a link valid for an hour. You can't watch it: judge motion from the filmstrip.

preview.description: Every direct save already returns a small contact sheet (four moments). false skips it; true or an object asks for a larger one with your choice of entry, moments, a filmstrip and test settings (parameter_values, where an image setting may be an upload id or a URL; param_tracks, actions, cues). With a project it shows a placed use of the entry with that element's own settings; with dry_run the unsaved code; without project_id a plain background. Nothing about the preview is saved.

project_id.description: Project the element is in. Needed with element_id.

scope.description: Only with animation 'new': one element, this project (the default with project_id; every scene of the video can import it), or the workspace library, only when the user asks to reuse it in other videos.

slug.description: Only with animation 'new': lowercase letters, digits and dashes; becomes @org/<slug>. Slugs are workspace-wide: one an animation of another project (or the library) holds is saved as the next free <slug>-N (the reply's animation and note say which, nothing to resend); one this project already holds is refused, naming it and a free slug.

target.description: Required when the animation is used outside this project: 'shared' changes it for everyone who updates, 'fork' copies it for this project first. Official and community animations always fork.

update_dependents.description: After a passing save, re-pin every animation that imports this one (a kit's scenes) to the new revision in the same call and move this project's uses of them; dependents_updated {report, project_uses_moved, note} says what moved. Left out: on for a project-scoped animation saved with project_id, off otherwise (a library animation's importers span the workspace: pass true).

upload_ids.description: Whole files sent with upload_file(file_names: [...]) and its one curl: each upload's file name is its path in the animation (e.g. 'entries/city.js'), and its text replaces or adds that file. Applied after files.

name: edit_animation
title: Edit an animation
